title: Making the World React Realistically: A Closed-Loop Interactive World Model for Autonomous Driving

output_modality.value: 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstruction rendered as surround-camera images (8 cameras), with background-vehicle trajectories and signal lights.

control_signal.value: Ego planner actions closing the loop on rendered images; background vehicles driven by learned policies (style latent, goal, map); signal light states set from each vehicle's planned intention.

control_mechanism.value: Style-conditioned imitation-learned vehicle policy fine-tuned with multi-agent GRPO in the closed loop; lights via LoRA fine-tuned one-step diffusion editor conditioned on lamp map and state map.

base_model.value: MTGS-based 3DGS reconstruction with Gaussian vehicle assets; mixture-of-experts policy with ODE-RNN style encoder; Difix one-step diffusion with LoRA for light editing.

datasets.value: Evaluated on 288 long-tail NAVSIM navtest failure scenarios from 89 nuPlan logs; policies imitation-learned on INTERACTION and fine-tuned on nuPlan navtrain.

metrics.value: JS divergence and histogram overlap of TTC, peak acceleration and relative speed; collision rate; route progress; PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS; VLM-read light state correctness.

controllability_evidence.value: Interaction realism against logs: mean JS 0.0074 versus 0.0485 for World Engine (85% lower); novel-view vehicle PSNR gain of 2.0 dB reported in abstract.

closed_loop.value: Yes; Alpamayo 1.5 ego planner reacts to rendered images and background vehicles respond, 12 steps at 0.5 s per episode.

notes: Not a generative control-signal model in the usual sense; control family is a best fit (closest to scenario or behaviour conditioning). Only future work is stated in the conclusion excerpt. Packet carries an arXiv date of 2026.
